title: Clinical Review Desk Reference: Approving a First-Time Quantity Limit Exception (Utilization Management Program)
content:
This reference covers the approval of a first-time quantity limit exception on an acute migraine drug under the Utilization Management Program — sumatriptan, Nurtec ODT or Ubrelvy — on the prescriber's clinical information on file.

## Governing rule

The approved quantity of a first-time quantity limit exception is not fixed until the records carry an undecided first-time quantity limit exception request for the drug.

The approved quantity per rolling 30 days is the quantity the Utilization Management Program determines for first-time quantity limit exceptions on acute migraine drugs. The authorization the approval puts in force takes effect on the decision date and runs the package's quantity limit approval months under the general approval-period rule of the program.

## What an approval records

One approval records the approval decision on the undecided first-time quantity limit exception case, with the reason `criteria_met` and the approved quantity, and records a new quantity limit authorization for the drug, produced by clinical review, carrying the approved quantity per rolling 30 days and its first and last days in force. Afterwards the case shows as approved and the member's authorizations list the new quantity limit authorization.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `approve_quantity_exception_611b3a5d`, an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. The approval is complete when the receipt shows status "approved".

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | the customer reference number of the member, as read from the customer profile lookup | identifier |
| `review_program_id` | the reference number of the member's Utilization Management Program, as read from the review program lookup | identifier |
| `source_case_id` | the reference number of the opening of the case being approved, as returned when the request was filed or as read from the review case lookup | identifier |
| `drug_name` | the drug of the case | one value of the drug list below |
| `approved_quantity_per_30` | the approved quantity of the drug per rolling 30 days | decimal units, up to 3 decimals |
| `effective_date` | the first day the authorization is in force | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `expiration_date` | the last day the authorization is in force | YYYY-MM-DD |

**`drug_name` values:** `atorvastatin`, `lisinopril`, `metformin`, `sertraline`, `levothyroxine`, `sumatriptan`, `oxycodone-acetaminophen`, `insulin glargine-yfgn`, `Lantus`, `Eliquis`, `Xarelto`, `Jardiance`, `Ozempic`, `Mounjaro`, `Wegovy`, `Zepbound`, `Trelegy Ellipta`, `Breztri Aerosphere`, `Nurtec ODT`, `Ubrelvy`, `Humira`, `adalimumab-adaz`, `Dupixent`, `Skyrizi`, `Rinvoq`, `Enbrel`, `Biktarvy`, `Ibrance`.

## Receipt

A successful call returns `decision_id` (the reference number of the approval decision on the case), `authorization_id` (the reference number of the new quantity limit authorization), `drug_name`, `approved_quantity_per_30` (up to 3 decimals), `effective_date` and `expiration_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and status "approved".

*Hypothetical illustration:* a call for `sumatriptan` with `approved_quantity_per_30` 12, `effective_date` 2026-03-10 and `expiration_date` 2026-09-09 returns a `decision_id`, an `authorization_id` and status "approved".
